en: A Memorial Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang of the Monastery Regarding the Presentation of Sūtras, Śāstras, and Other Works.
The Śramaṇa Xuanzang states: Xuanzang has heard that since the diagrams of the Yellow Emperor (Fuxi) were displayed, the use of written characters first began. As for the script of Zhuanzi...
The text is thus elucidated;
herein lies a magnificent and sublime model,
serving merely to instruct in righteousness and assist in the cultivation of virtue.
To record emotions and summarize nature,
one remains entangled amidst the dust of worldly burdens,
yet has not emerged beyond the boundaries of the mundane realm.
How could it compare to the secret instructions from the Dragon Palace and the subtle words from Vulture Peak,
which guide the masses of deluded beings throughout the realms of sand?
They have sheltered the passing of kalpas within the dust of the world.
Thus, the ultimate reality is formless;
it is the Dharma King who unfolds its source.
The ultimate truth is beyond words;
it is the Sage Emperors who have expounded its Way.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty has succeeded to the numinous mandate and emerged from the position of the Son of Heaven.
He assisted the destiny of the age and ascended to the pivot of power;
his excellence flourished throughout the nine seas,
and he strode alone, eclipsing the entire court.
His brilliance flies to the eight extremities;
he surveys the heights with the majesty of Xuanyuan and Haohao.
He divides his banners across the Purple Barrier.
He cut off the rebels at Youling and halted his imperial carriage at Qingqiu,
sweeping away the miasma of demonic influence from Panmu.
Military prowess having been brought to rest,
horses were returned to Mount Hua;
civil virtue was then proclaimed far and wide.
The Mandate was received at Mount Wan;
thereupon, the records were engraved upon the Yange library,
and the Lirong Terrace was established.
The phoenix-script calligraphy and tortoise-patterned inscriptions already flourish in the Dongguan Library;
the silver hooks and jade characters likewise cleanse the impurities of the Nangong Palace.
Yet, one still yearns for the True Suchness (Tathatā).
He reverently contemplates emptiness and stillness,
propagating and proclaiming the wondrous Dharma as his great instruction.
Consequently,
the discourse of Deer Park was retranslated in response to the auspicious occasion of the Sage’s advent.
The scholars of Kimmara,
looking up to his divine transformation, have come to pay their respects;
they have established the City of Fragrance upon the Central Continent.
The profound ford was drawn to the divine prefecture; thus,
the teaching of the Buddha’s image spread to the East,
reaching its greatest flourishing.
Xuanzang’s conduct has been without record;
by chance, it was fulfilled through the subtle workings of the Dao. I have mistakenly been numbered among the ranks of the black-robed clergy.
Feeling a sense of shame before the sages of antiquity,
he was moved by indignation and resolved to propagate [the teachings].
Relying upon the majesty of the state,
he traveled afar to seek out sacred traces.
This occurred in the past, in the Western Regions.
He personally practiced the Sanskrit language,
delved into the profound principles of the Vinaya,
and explored the esoteric treasury of the Āgamas.
The Sanskrit manuscripts of sutras and śāstras obtained totaled one thousand cases,
comprising six hundred and fifty-seven works,
along with seven Buddha statues.
There were one hundred and fifty grains of the Buddha’s flesh relics,
along with a casket containing bone relics and other items. Thereupon,
he prepared his equipment for the journey to the Golden Land (Suvarṇabhūmi).
Setting out from Yumen,
he reverently received the imperial decree and proceeded to undertake the translation.
Thereupon, a group of śrāvakas was convened;
together they investigated the meaning of wisdom,
engaging in contemplation for an extended period.
It has not yet been completed in its entirety;
those portions seen by the scribe total fifty-eight fascicles.
The Mahābodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra in twenty fascicles;
the Buddhagotra-sūtra in one fascicle;
and the Ṣaṇmukha-dhāraṇī-sūtra in one fascicle.

The *Xianyang shengjiao lun* (Treatise on the Manifestation of the Holy Teachings) in twenty fascicles and the *Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (Great Vehicle Abhidharma Compendium Commentary) in sixteen fascicles were compiled into eight bundles.
I have transcribed [the texts] as specified elsewhere,
along with the aforementioned śarīra relics, Buddha images, and Sanskrit manuscripts of sūtras and śāstras;
I respectfully present them for Your Majesty’s acceptance at the palace gate.
However, Your Majesty’s sagely discernment illuminates all,
and your profound words are deep and far-reaching;
as for Xuanzang, my learning is not hidden or esoteric.
I, Shi Xie, offer this eulogy for your thorough understanding.
How can I fail to look up to and praise your celestial regulations,
and reverently propagate the ultimate teaching?
It is also like a flickering torch casting its light against the vast expanse of the sun, or a slender,
meandering stream [flowing toward the great ocean].
Having crossed the vast abyss and achieved greatness,
I am filled with remorse and tremble with fear,
as if treading upon ice or entering a deep valley.
Respectfully submitted.

On the thirteenth day of the seventh month in the twentieth year of the Zhenguan era, the śramaṇa Xuanzang presents this memorial to the Emperor regarding the *Records of the Western Regions*. Memorial by the śramaṇa Xuanzang: Xuanzang addresses the Throne.
The coiled trees of Youling and the Cloud-Office were recorded as the territories of Emperor Xuan;
the shifting sands and the blue seas were noted by Xia as the domains of Yao.
The Baihuan of the Western Qiang offer tribute to the sovereign who wears his robes with ease;
the Chuefu of the Eastern Yi likewise do so.
The sovereign who placed bribery under lock and key has truly spread his brilliance through past ages and established his enduring legacy in former canons.
I humbly observe that Your Majesty grasps the cosmic order and rides upon the opportune moment;
you hold the balance and provide a model for all things.
You have carved the boats and strung the bows.
He awes the world and brings salvation to all living beings.
Like the legs of the giant turtle and the ashes of the reed, he fills the square earth and patches the circular heavens.
He displays martial prowess through the seven virtues of statecraft.
He propagated the civilizing teachings throughout the ten human relations,
blending the leaking springs back into their source;
his transformation reached even the *piao* grass and the *wei* reeds.
The fragrant herbs send forth their brilliance;
the waves of the well open into blossoms.
In the pleasure grove, the tigers are tamed.
Nests soar among the peaks as the musical pitch resonates;
purple grease floats upon the ritual vessels,
while white clouds drift over the jade-bound tablets.
Thus, it enabled [the sun] to traverse the *ruòmù* tree and pool at the *méngfǎn* marshes;
to drench the blazing fires and illuminate the accumulated ice;
and to ascend the Red Slope to receive the breath of the North.
Crossing the Cangjin Ferry, they presented their tribute;
yet the records of former worthies have been lost,
and the accounts from the old archives have vanished.
How could it compare to the Han dynasty, when Guan and Zhang were close to Jincheng in Ganlu,
or the Qin guards at Guilin, which merely reached Zhupu? Fortunately for Xuanzang,
we have been blessed by the upright governance of Heaven and Earth during the Zhenguan era, while both the Chinese and the barbarians enjoy tranquility.
With my mind darkened by the realm of Brahma,
how could I dare to match those who pursue worldly excellence?
My life is as fleeting as morning dew.
My strength is like that of autumn locusts;
I can only rely above on the Imperial Spirit and draw support below from the lives of common insects.
Thus, I cast off my body and set forth upon this journey.
Seeking the distant from the near,
they have wandered through regions where prostrations are performed with palms joined,
and have drifted among lands beyond the reach of multiple translations.
The giant magpies of Tiaozhi verify what was previously heard;
the solitary luan birds of Jibin [confirm what has long been known].
Returning to examine past realities:
as time shifts and years accumulate,
human desires increasingly follow the ways of the heavens.
Thus, he was able to descend from the snowy peaks to sail upon the Tīrthika River,
and to reach the Crane Forest to dwell upon Vulture Peak. Yet,
the path to Jetavana remains but as a winding trace in the void.
The king abandoned this site, and it became accessible for ascent.
He sought it out and toured it;
as the seasons passed, he spoke of returning to the imperial capital.
Suddenly, two cycles of twelve years have passed;
the lands I have heard of and traversed number one hundred and thirty-eight.
I venture to say:
The vast expanse of the earth traversed by Zhanghai is now but an empty boast;
the heights scaled by Kuafu are likewise a mere legend.
There is no description of its climate and soil.
Ban Chao was enfeoffed as a marquis yet remained far from it;
Zhang Qian gazed upon it, yet his knowledge was not comprehensive.
As for what Xuanzang has recorded,
it is somewhat more detailed and exhaustive;
its circuitous phrasing and grandiloquent descriptions have been largely pruned away.
I have compiled this as the *Great Tang Records on the Western Regions* in twelve fascicles;
the transcription is as presented elsewhere.
Xuanzang is of dull and ignorant nature.
Being dim-sighted in compiling the facts,
I look forward to the right-hand pen [of Your Majesty] bestowing its grace and adorning them with the left-hand words [of your edict].
I shall truncate these verbose words and extract the essential records,
thereby designating him as the foremost among the hundred sovereigns.
I hereby record these nine hills for this august era,
hoping that the hidden splendors of the *Shan jing* (Classic of Mountains) may be transmitted through this work and its recondite brilliance concealed herein.
I am unable to restrain my humble and earnest devotion.
I respectfully approach the palace gate to present this offering,
fearing that it may lightly disturb Your Majesty’s imperial presence;
I am deeply filled with trepidation and anxiety.
Respectfully submitted.
A Petition Requesting Emperor Taizong Wenhuang to Compose a Preface for the Scripture and to Inscribe the Title of the Scripture. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang says: [The petition follows].
I, Xuanzang, have long been enrolled among the ranks of the Mysterious Gate;
fortunately, I have encountered this flourishing era and hope to hear the Ultimate Way.
Wandering his mind through the banquet of the Dharma,
he constantly lamented that the sacred texts of the Perfectly Enlightened One were not yet fully detailed or complete;
thus, he was moved by a profound sense of longing and admiration.
Wandering through distant lands,
we rely far and wide upon the imperial majesty;
our hope is that all shall be saved.
In the second month of last year, I received an imperial decree to translate these texts.
Now, five sections have been completed,
totaling fifty-eight fascicles.
Copied as elsewhere.
I have observed that when the honored images at Hongfu Monastery were first completed,
His Majesty personally descended from his imperial carriage to visit them.
Opening the eyes of the blue lotus,
I now venture to rely on this principle as new translations of the sūtras and śāstras have appeared.
I humbly pray that Your Majesty will graciously deign to inscribe the title of this scripture with your divine calligraphy.
Your Majesty has graciously composed this profound literary work, its preface elucidating the ultimate principle of the Way;
we hope that these celestial writings and secret thoughts will shine with the same brilliance as the sun and moon.
With characters like jade and hooks like silver, they shall be as enduring as heaven and earth;
thus, for ten generations hence, their praise and chanting shall be inexhaustible,
and for a thousand years beyond, the gaze of veneration shall never cease.
Unable to restrain the utmost sincerity of my devotion,
I respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty’s perusal.
I fear I have presumptuously offended Your Imperial Majesty.
I prostrate myself, overcome with trepidation and perspiration. This is my humble submission.
The Imperial Edict of Emperor Taizong Wenhuang in Response to the Request for a Preface to the Scripture. The Edict: Your humble servant has fully understood the intent of your communication.
The Dharma Master had long been distinguished for his lofty conduct;
early on, he emerged beyond the mundane world.
He launched the precious vessel to reach the other shore.
He sought out the wondrous Way and opened the gates of the Dharma;
he propagated and expounded the Great Design,
sweeping away all manner of transgressions.
Therefore, the Cloud of Compassion desires to roll up and spread out its shade over the four voids;
the Sun of Wisdom intends to dispel the darkness with its radiance across the eight extremities.
Is it not only the Dharma Master who can cause this radiance to spread?
My learning is shallow and my mind is clumsy;
I am still deluded regarding the nature of things,
let alone the profound and subtle mysteries of the Buddha-dharma.
How could anyone possibly fathom it from above?
I request that you provide the title for this scripture;
it is not something I have heard before.
Furthermore, it says: "The newly compiled *Record of the Western Regions* should be read by [the Emperor] himself.
An imperial edict was issued to bestow this upon Dharma Master Xuanzang from within the palace.
A Memorial in Response to the Imperial Edict from Emperor Taizong Wenhuang. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang addresses Your Majesty:
I have humbly received the imperial edict written in ink.
I have humbly received your gracious encouragement and instructions;
I shall reverently uphold your imperial decree and maintain my practice with unwavering diligence.
Xuanzang is truly prostrate with awe and trepidation.
Xuanzang’s learning remains shallow and sparse; it was by mere misfortune that he joined the ranks of the Dharma companions.
Fortunately, the nine seas are now unified and the four quarters are free from anxiety;
thus we rely on imperial majesty to launch this distant expedition.
Relying on the majesty of his nation, he sought the Way;
he traveled to distant lands and braved perilous terrain,
though his sincere devotion was but that of a fool.
Those who admire the extraordinary and cherish the remote truly rely upon the civilizing influence of the Imperial Court.
The sutras and śāstras they have obtained shall be translated by imperial decree.
I have seen that these works exist as scrolls,
yet they lack a systematic arrangement.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty’s sagely thoughts are as vast as spreading clouds.
Celestial flowers and auspicious scenes blaze forth;
its principles encompass the patterns of the cosmos,
and its phrasing surpasses that of the Xian-ying music.
His fame soars across a thousand ages,
and his achievements eclipse those of a hundred sovereigns.
I humbly consider that his supernormal powers are boundless.
It is not that my divine intellect is insufficient to expound its principles;
rather, the Holy Teaching is profound and remote.
Were it not for the sublime prose of the Sage, how could its origins be set forth?
Therefore, I have ventured to offend Your Majesty’s august authority by daring to hope for a preface; yet Your Imperial gaze remains distant and lofty,
and You have not deigned to grant me Your compassionate favor.
Reflecting upon myself with repeated thought, I look about me and lose all sense of purpose.
I, Xuanzang, have heard that the sun and moon adorn the heavens.
Having already distributed its radiance through doors and windows,
it also flows with moisture upon the crags and shores, where the rivers mark the earth.
The music of Yunhe and Guangle does not withhold its resonance from the deaf and ignorant;
the wondrous treasures within golden walls do not remain hidden.
How could its brilliant colors be hidden from the ignorant and blind?
Daring to rely on this principle,
I again offer my earnest prayer.
I humbly entreat that your clouds and rain may descend in grace,
and your celestial brilliance look down from on high,
so that you may be paired with the Two Polarities and endure for all eternity.
It hangs suspended together with the two luminaries.
Thus, the subtle words from Vulture Peak were made far-reaching by relying upon the divine brush.
The profound mysteries of the Kukkutārāma are proclaimed through sublime rhetoric;
how could they concern merely the limited assembly of Brahmā?
I alone have been graced with such honor and prosperity;
as for the deluded masses of living beings,
they are only now beginning to transcend the burdens of worldly dust.
With the utmost sincerity and earnestness,
I respectfully approach the imperial palace to present this memorial for Your Majesty’s perusal. I am deeply aware that I have presumptuously offended Your Imperial Majesty.
I prostrate myself in deep trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.
A Memorial of Thanks for Receiving the Kāṣāya and Razor. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang.
I have reverently received the Imperial Decree bestowing one cassock and one razor of fine steel.
Your gracious favor descends like clouds and rain.
I have erroneously been graced by the abundant dew of imperial favor;
my life has been blessed with such profound and generous magnanimity that I am filled with trepidation and awe as I strive to maintain it with utmost sincerity.
Fortunately, I, Xuanzang, have encountered the civilizing influence of the enlightened era and early joined the ranks of those who have stilled their minds;
yet my three karmic actions remain without discipline.
The four debts of gratitude remain unpaid;
yet Your Majesty’s regard has not forsaken me,
and the descent of your grace and honor has reached down upon me.
The robe of patience contains the radiance of flowing dawn clouds;
the sword of wisdom is sharper than that which cuts jade.
I shall reverently don it to subdue the demons of affliction.
Wearing [this] to sever the net of worldly toil,
I have already provoked the censure of others;
fearing that my merits are hollow and sparse for having presumed upon your grace.
I have presumptuously received this extraordinary honor;
I am filled with shame and trepidation,
overwhelmed by the utmost sense of awe and gratitude.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
Having defiled Your Celestial Inspection,
I am deeply trembling with trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.

Memorial of Thanks for the "Preface to the Holy Teachings of the Tripitaka" composed by Emperor Taizong Wenhuang. Memorial of Thanks for the "Preface to the Holy Teachings of the Tripitaka" composed by Emperor Taizong Wenhuang. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang speaks.
I have humbly heard that the six lines of the hexagrams explore the profound mysteries,
yet they are confined to the realm of birth and extinction;
while the hundred things have their names correctly established.
Having not yet entered the realm of True Suchness (tathatā), one still remains distant from its subtle meanings; yet by examining the profound texts, one perceives that their depths are unfathomable.
Looking back with lofty imagination upon the imperial charts of antiquity, all successive selections of sages have returned to this same principle.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty, the Emperor, has manifested as the substance of the jade-hair [Buddha],
and governs the heavens as the Golden Wheel-turning King.
You have expanded the nine provinces of the former kings.
It eclipses the suns and moons of a hundred thousand worlds,
surpasses the territories of successive dynasties,
and encompasses the dharma-realm as vast as the sands of the Ganges.
Consequently, the Jetavana Vihāra was incorporated into the imperial domain,
and the sacred texts upon palm leaves were all returned to the Imperial Library.
Previously, Xuanzang had traveled to the Kukkuṭapāda Mountain, merely to pay his respects there while shaking his mendicant’s staff.
Traveling ten thousand *li* along the way,
one relies on the Heavenly Majesty as if it were but a few paces away;
it is not by riding upon a thousand-petaled lotus that this is achieved.
He proceeded to the Twin Śāla Trees in the time it takes to eat a meal;
there he searched through and expounded the Tripiṭaka,
exhausting all that was stored within the Dragon Palace.
Having researched the One Vehicle and exhausted the bequeathed teachings of Vulture Peak,
they have all been recorded in these written forms.
He returned to present [the texts] at the Purple Palace (Zichen).
Shortly thereafter, he received an imperial edict granting him permission to translate them.
Xuanzang’s understanding falls short of that of Nāgārjuna;
I have mistakenly received the honor of transmitting the Lamp of the Dharma,
yet my talent is not equal to that of Aśvaghoṣa.
I am deeply ashamed that my skill in transcribing [the texts] is insufficient;
the errors and discrepancies in the translated sūtras and śāstras are particularly numerous.
Thus, I have come to receive the grace of Heaven.
He applied his mind with care to compose the preface;
its prose transcends the realm of the *Xici* and the *Xuan*,
like the sun gathering its thousand rays of light.
Its principle encompasses the gateway to all wonders;
it is like the Dharma-cloud that moistens the hundred grasses.
To hear its single voice expounded is a rare encounter even after billions of kalpas.
Suddenly, with this fragile life, I have personally heard the sound of the Brahma-voice;
I leap for joy and rejoice as if hearing my own prediction of enlightenment (vyākaraṇa),
unable to contain the height of my gratitude and delight.

I respectfully submit this memorial to the palace gate to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge of it. I humbly state. Imperial Rescript from Emperor Taizong Wenhuang in Response to Dharma Master Xuanzang’s Memorial of Thanks. Imperial Rescript: My talent falls short of the excellence of jade ornaments. My virtue is insufficient to match the brilliance of refined gems. Yet, by relying on the power of the Buddha’s grace, I have succeeded in pacifying the four quarters and bringing the eight directions under my rule. Now that the great enterprise of the Dharma has been restored, I have received the Master’s letter of thanks. I am deeply moved by his sincerity and profoundly grateful for his devotion. I hereby grant him the title of “Great Master of the Three Treasures” (Sanbao Dashi). Let this be known. [The Emperor] further decreed: "The Master has traveled through distant lands to seek the sublime teachings. His hardships were immense, yet his resolve remained firm. He has brought back the true scriptures, thereby benefiting all sentient beings. This is truly a rare achievement. I shall bestow upon him a purple robe and the rank of State Preceptor (Guoshi). Thus, the imperial favor was bestowed, and the Master’s reputation spread throughout the realm. The Master, in turn, submitted a memorial of thanks, which the Emperor received with great appreciation. The Emperor’s response was as follows: "Your journey to the West was undertaken for the sake of the Dharma. You braved the perils of the road and endured the hardships of the journey. That you have now returned with the sacred texts is a source of great joy to me. I shall ensure that the teachings you have brought are propagated far and wide, so that all may partake in their benefits. Thus, the Emperor’s decree was issued, and the Master’s mission was fully realized. The imperial edict was proclaimed, and the Master was honored with the highest distinction. The entire court and the people alike rejoiced at the manifestation of the Emperor’s piety and the flourishing of the Buddhist faith. [End of Document]
It is said that although he was broad-minded and erudite,
he was particularly unacquainted with the Buddhist scriptures.
I composed the preface yesterday;
it is deeply crude and clumsy.
I fear only that my defiled brushwork may pollute the golden tablets.
To point out rubble among a grove of pearls—
suddenly I have received your letter,
for which I am unworthily honored by your praise.
Cultivating my person and examining my thoughts,
I find only increasing cause for shame;
my virtues are insufficient to be praised.
Your kind thanks are but a weary labor.
A Memorial of Thanks for the "Preface to the Record of the Holy Teachings. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang.
I venture to say:
Those who recognize the truth are few;
I have always lamented the road leading eastward,
for those who lose their way are many.
One must rely on a borrowed south-pointing chariot;
how much more so when the Great Way is profound and remote,
and the wondrous gate is empty and still?
Were it not for one of transcendent wisdom,
who could possibly provide this exposition?
I humbly reflect upon this.
His Imperial Highness the Crown Prince embodies the majesty of the Celestial Pole,
and his benevolence extends like the springtime.
He illuminates the sun of the Buddha with renewed brilliance and succeeds to the Wheel of Dharma as it was about to fall;
the bridge for crossing over now has its rightful master.
The lamp of the Dharma remains here.
Xuanzang is determined to exhaustively master the Buddha-way,
vowing to sacrifice his very body and life.
Ever since arriving from the eastern lands,
I have aspired to reach the Western Regions;
may the Imperial Spirit protect and sustain me.
I obtained six hundred and fifty-seven treatises and sūtras.
Subsequently, I was graced by an imperial edict ordering me, Xuanzang, to translate them.
Thereupon, Your Majesty deigned to bestow your compassionate decree and composed this preface,
spreading the clouds of mercy throughout the kalpas of dust.
He pours down the gracious rain upon the realms of sand;
Your Highness wields the blade of mastery over the Tripiṭaka and reverently propagates the ten wholesome deeds.
Furthermore, he composed the *Śāstrasaṃvarṇana* (Record Praising the Sage),
illuminating the Great Way and clarifying the gateway to the true nature (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
Thus, that which exists is not taken as existing;
when discussing the realm of emptiness and stillness,
even emptiness itself is empty.
He has already attained the divine mind,
far transcending the realm beyond all bonds;
as for Xuanzang, he has not yet clarified the turbid waters.
Having suddenly obtained this bright pearl,
I shall reverently receive it upon my head and uphold it,
forever making it a mirror for my mind.
Unable to contain my humble feelings of profound trepidation and gratitude,
I respectfully submit this letter to express my thanks for your information.
Respectfully submitted.

The Emperor’s Letter from the Spring Palace Reporting to Dharma Master Xuanzang; The Emperor’s Letter from the Spring Palace Reporting to Dharma Master Xuanzang in Response to His Letter of Thanks: "I have always lacked talent and learning."
By nature, I am not quick-witted;
I have not yet perused the various texts of the Inner Canon (Buddhist scriptures).
Consequently, the prefaces to the treatises I have composed are particularly vulgar, clumsy, and prolix.
Suddenly, I saw the letter you sent,
which praised and extolled me;
I looked upon myself and reflected.
Feeling both shame and trepidation,
and further reflecting on the great effort taken by the Master to travel from afar,
he was deeply ashamed; he then issued an edict to confer [the title] upon Dharma Master Xuanzang.
A Letter from the Long-lived Brahmin to Dharma Master Xuanzang, by Emperor Taizong Wenhuang: "The Creator fashions all things with impartiality."
Lives vary in length;
heaven and earth cover and sustain all.
The ignorant and the wise are born alike.
Thus we know that supreme sages and supreme worthies have appeared in every age;
nevertheless, it is rare for successive kings and emperors to encounter them.
Reflecting upon myself, I find my virtue meager and my conduct slight;
my wisdom is faint and my power shallow.
Fortunately, by virtue of past affinities and auspicious fortune, I have been able to encounter a True Man.
Since taking the aphrodisiacs,
my hands and feet have gradually become weak and impaired;
I must therefore exercise even greater care and prudence.
I hope to achieve complete eradication [of my ailments].
I rejoice in consoling my exhausted body,
yet I feel much shame for having relied upon divine prescriptions.
Relying solely on subsequent medicine for my life,
I hope that longevity may be expected;
I truly look forward to transcending this brief world and existing forever.
The countenance remains ever-vigilant and does not decay;
the hair that has turned white changes from pale to black,
and the body that was worn out is rid of its decline and becomes vigorous once more.
Can this heart and this vow be fulfilled?
I shall only exhaust my profound sincerity and respectfully await your excellent method.
Presented by Neichu to Dharma Master Xuanzang.

A Memorial Requesting the Circulation of Sūtras and Śāstras submitted by Dharma Master Xuanzang. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang says: [The memorial continues: "I, Xuanzang, have traveled through various regions to seek the Dharma. Having obtained numerous sūtras and śāstras, I now respectfully submit them to the Imperial Court. I pray that Your Majesty will graciously permit their circulation so that the True Dharma may spread throughout the realm. [End of Memorial]
I humbly submit that the profound principles of the Way have no manifest signs;
it is through the teachings of names and instruction that they are transmitted as a legacy for posterity.
The Dharma is fundamentally unconditioned;
it relies upon words and symbols to bring about transformation.
Thus we know that the employment of names and teachings is the skillful means of the Dharma King.
To elucidate words and symbols is the capable task of sagely sovereigns.
Were it not for those with the far-reaching vision of the three penetrations and the humble salvation of the four great vows,
who could possibly sustain the movement of the golden wheel?
Is he not one who propagates the teaching of the expansive white tuft?
We humbly observe that Your Majesty, the Emperor, has attained sagehood through disciplined cultivation,
and embodies the Way with reverent clarity.
He革除 (transformed) corrupt customs and垂 (established) a transformation of harmony and concord;
his moral influence and instruction reached throughout the three thousand worlds.
His domain extends across ten billion worlds;
facing the eightfold governance, he yokes his carriage,
and driving the five vehicles, he gallops forth.
He set aside his traces beyond the mundane world to occupy a position within the realm; thus,
the four seas were free from anxiety.
In his leisure from the myriad affairs of state,
he stored the treasures of wisdom in the Qilin Hall and drew the waters of insight from the Dragon Palace.
Xuanzang’s karma has forfeited his capacity for thorough understanding,
and his learning is insufficient to rival that of the ancients;
yet, he reverently receives this imperial decree.
I have translated the Sanskrit text in detail;
yet looking inward at my own mediocrity and folly,
I fear I may have deviated from the profound intent.
Reflecting deeply upon my sincere intentions,
I fear they might harm the Great Way;
therefore, I have been diligent and untiring from dawn until night.
Body and mind are free from indolence.
Wherever the Imperial transformation extends,
there is no error in the teaching of the single voice.
Blessed by divine favor,
a single heart’s resonance caused the bright sun to turn back three stations in its course.
My sincere devotion has moved the hearing of the Ninefold Heavens;
thus, Your Majesty has graciously bestowed Your divine mind to arrange and clarify the holy teachings.
The peaks of his eloquence have cut through the Han lands;
he has already shaken the palace of the Lord of Śākyas.
The ocean of his meaning floats to the heavens.
As the invitation of Brahmā was about to be issued,
the Great Teachings of the Muni were thus illuminated and proclaimed through the support of sacred literary elegance.
The subtle words of Prajñāpāramitā rely upon imperial edicts to be brilliantly propagated; yet,
in secluded dwellings and humble customs, [they remain obscure].
Having never heard the sound of the Brahma-voice,
how could this remote and desolate frontier behold the splendor of the celestial constellations?
Once the translation of the sutras and śāstras was completed,
he requested that the *Preface to the Holy Teachings of the Tripiṭaka* composed by the Emperor and the *Record of the Sage* written by the Crown Prince be prefixed to them.
Proclaim this far and near,
so that all may hear and know it throughout the great prefectures and famous provinces.
Bestow one copy upon each;
thus the Way shall not be practiced in vain,
and the Dharma shall encounter no obstruction.
The clouds of wisdom spread far and wide;
the rain of Dharma falls upon all within and without.
May the Imperial Spirit enjoy the blessings of this gift of the Dharma.
Forever and ever without end,
the common people shall abound in the utility of the wealth of the Dharma;
in every rebirth, none shall be left behind.
Unable to restrain my utmost sincerity,
I respectfully submit this memorial to present my petition for Your Majesty’s consideration.
I humbly pray that Your Heavenly Compassion will deign to show favor and grant my request.
I humbly submit this for your perusal;
I am filled with trepidation as I reflect upon it.
Respectfully stated.

A Memorial Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang to the Crown Prince, Expressing Gratitude for the Letter Sent with the "Account of the Sage" (*Shushengji*). The Śramaṇa Xuanzang respectfully submits this memorial.
The Imperial Messenger has graced us with his presence;
we humbly receive your enlightened decree, which has descended personally upon this lowly and insignificant person.
In recording these accounts of the Sage,
you have graciously bestowed your profound grace, so that its far-reaching influence permeates even the most subtle and obscure realms.
Receiving this gracious mandate with profound reverence, I am filled with awe and trepidation.
I humbly consider that as the sun and moon traverse the heavens, their illumination shines brightly before the divine mirror.
The sages and worthies expound their transformations, yet they flourish only when met with responsive conditions.
Thus, the True Teaching is practiced during enlightened times,
and the Great Instruction arises under auspicious fortunes.
This is not the celebration of a single individual; how could its benefits fail to reach even the most remote and desolate regions?
This is not the illumination of the wisdom of the three insights (trividyā).
How could one clarify what is obscure and dark?
We humbly beseech Your Highness, the Crown Prince, to immerse your spirit in the waters of wisdom and cleanse your nature in the profound currents.
His virtue illuminates the clouds of Yao;
his brilliance continues the light, increasing its clarity.
His achievements shine forth, bestowed by Heaven itself.
His learning penetrates the mysteries of the Three Vehicles;
his realization rivals innate wisdom;
and his talent encompasses the agility of the four types of eloquence.
As for opening up the charts and displaying the traces,
their subtlety exhausts the eight calligraphic styles;
they depart from the conventional texts to discern one's aspirations.
Its principles synthesize the Nine Categories;
the movement of its brushstrokes drifts like clouds,
and the peaks of its phrasing are saturated with mist.
It encompasses the transformations of the six lines of the hexagrams;
it wields the brush to illuminate the light of the Three Luminaries.
It brings down the secret blossoms of the Jia-observation.
He expounded the profound essence of the Jeta Grove;
his thoughts were like wind and clouds,
and his clarity hung like the sun and moon.
The influence of this pure transformation reaches all;
the common people receive its blessings,
and its grace extends to both the hidden and the manifest realms.
The celebration pervades both humans and devas;
we cannot contain our profound sense of joy.
We respectfully submit this letter of thanks for your information.
Respectfully submitted.
A Petition for the Translation and Circulation of the Scriptures. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang.
I humbly consider that:
The traces of the six lines are laid out to examine the hidden influences of yin and yang;
the eight trigrams form their images.
Examining the errors and deficiencies of the sun and moon,
and how the wondrous eloquence beyond words has spread the Ultimate Way to humans and devas,
while the grand regulations of the full letters have caused flourishing achievements to soar through both emptiness and existence.
He rescued those submerged in mutual ruin and discerned the current of those who have lost their way in youth;
as for his power of selection and rejection, how could it be compared to others?
I humbly observe that Your Highness, the Crown Prince, harbors inner brilliance and nurtures virtue;
by nature you possess manifold talents,
and your reputation for benevolence overflows to the myriad nations.
His compassionate heart remained fixed upon the Triple Gem;
he profoundly fathomed the provisional and the ultimate,
and wondrously mastered form and emptiness.
Without acting, the Way flourishes;
by forgetting oneself, merit becomes manifest.
Lowering one's will, one succeeds in the Great Flourishing.
Pay close attention to this praise and exposition;
it is like a great bell awaiting a strike,
or like an empty valley that will surely respond.
He elucidated the subtle imagery through names and phrases,
and fully expressed the profound means through vocal teachings;
he subsequently illuminated them with the torch of wisdom.
He ferries them across by means of the boat of wisdom;
having illuminated the darkness of the long night,
he rescues those drowning in the violent torrent.
The three paths of suffering find prosperity and fortune;
the four modes of birth receive reliance and support.
How auspicious for the Mysterious Gate!
Fortunate indeed are the monastics;
yet the common people of the borderlands have not yet beheld the splendor of the Sage Emperor,
and how could the humble and lowly masses hear the teachings of the Perfect and Universal [Buddha]?
Beneath the heavens, all share the shade of Yao’s clouds;
yet the customs of distant lands have not yet been moistened by the Dharma rain.
Xuanzang has partaken of the harmonious and gracious benefits [of the imperial bounty].
I have reverently studied the profound instructions and respectfully received the imperial edicts,
and with devotion translated the Sanskrit scriptures.
A Response: The Imperial Spirit has composed this chapter, prefacing the teaching of True Suchness;
Your Majesty has turned your sagely thoughts toward it and exerted your literary brilliance.
Expounding the doctrine of the true nature of reality,
all living beings without exception rejoice in its great reliance.
How much more so for those who have personally received its moistening grace—
how could they not leap for joy upon seeing the translated sūtras and śāstras?
Please circulate this externally for distribution.
May it open the eye of wisdom for all sentient beings and spread the clouds of compassion over all living creatures.
May those who follow the discarded teachings likewise receive benefit and joy,
as may the people of this world who have lost their way.
We have all traveled far to seek instruction. Driven by the utmost sincerity,
we respectfully submit this memorial to present our request for your consideration.
I humbly present this for your perusal as if it were a speck of dust; I am deeply moved by trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.

A Letter of Thanks for the Emperor’s Copying of the *Ṣaṇmukha-dhāraṇī* and His Inscription on the *Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra* While He Was in the Spring Palace. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang respectfully submits this.
The Imperial Messenger has condescended to visit us;
his gracious command is most profound and abundant.

We have humbly received one scroll of the *Ṣaṇmukhī-dhāraṇī-sūtra* transcribed by Your Majesty’s divine brush, as well as the sixty-six scrolls of the *Mahābodhisattva-piṭaka-sūtra* and other texts, all bearing Your Majesty’s own inscriptions.
An extraordinary favor has suddenly descended;
I am struck with trepidation, reflecting only upon my own faults. Your gracious bounty shines forth, encompassing all.
I rejoice as if ascending a high peak.
I humbly consider that the ultimate teaching is subtle and ineffable.
Principle emerges from beyond the profound and obscure;
the mysterious chapters soar loftily.
The Way is expounded amidst words and symbols.
Manifestation and concealment follow the times;
movement and withdrawal depend on the cosmic cycles.
These do not belong to the transformation of pure harmony alone.
How could this not be the propagation of the profound and subtle teachings?
We humbly reflect that Your Highness, the Crown Prince, possesses virtue as vast as heaven and earth,
and your Way shines with the brilliance of the full moon.
The Three Honored Ones have stilled their minds;
the myriad realms look up to them with hope.
They spread the clouds of wisdom to provide shade for the burning house.
Beating the Dharma-drum to awaken those on the dark path,
they are drenched by a great downpour of grace and transcendently delivered across the abyss.
Indeed, how could the sincerity of using skin for paper and bone for pens ever suffice to express it?
It is the vow to sacrifice one's life and follow [the Master] unto death.
Looking back upon those many who feel shame,
this is truly a gathering of auspiciousness through imperial spirit,
forever guiding the destiny of the Golden Wheel.
May your blessings nourish your holy virtue,
so that you may swiftly succeed to the station of the Jade Tuft.
As for Xuanzang, I examine my own nature and find it mediocre and unworthy.
Observing this auspicious occasion of the Way,
my birth is insignificant and my capacity shallow;
I vainly bear the weight of this profound honor.
I cannot contain my utmost joy and exultation.
I respectfully submit this letter to express my gratitude for your information. I beg you to overlook its brevity and informality in your perusal.
I prostrate myself in profound trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial.

A Memorial by Dharma Master Xuanzang Requesting that Articles for Inquiries and a Letter Be Sent to the Western Regions The Śramaṇa Xuanzang states: [Memorial] requesting that articles for inquiries and a letter be sent to the Western Regions.
I have heard that when the Way flourishes, it covers and sustains all;
its merit is profound and its transformation vast.
Virtue pacifies both those within and without;
thus, those nearby are reverent and those afar are at peace. Therefore:
It hangs down as the teaching of Heaven and establishes itself as the transformation of the Earth;
this is truly the great governing principle for all things.
This is the Great Canon for governing the universe.
We humbly observe that Your Majesty, the Emperor,
is endowed with the brilliant radiance of the profound celestial phenomena.
Although the supreme virtue of the Great Earth sustains all things and fashions the categories of beings,
it is [the Buddha] who brilliantly elucidates the eternal principles of human relations.
The regions of those who wear robes fastened on the left sent tributes through successive translations;
the customs of those with reversed tongues likewise did so.
I request that the officials change their tones.
Were it not for one whose virtue penetrates the spirits and whose benevolence covers both the hidden and the manifest,
how could the mists be cleared from the layered barriers and the winds sweep away these remote frontiers?
I, Xuanzang, formerly relied upon the imperial power to seek the Way in distant lands and reverently received the words of the Dharma.
He took the study of the Brahma-lore to heart,
extensively investigating the origins of names and characteristics,
and inquired deeply into the principles of the provisional and the ultimate.
Having come here to propagate and translate [the scriptures], they have duly accorded with the profound instructions;
this has moved the Imperial heart above.
He once again elucidated the Way of Vulture Peak and reverently upheld the Buddha’s intent;
he further expounded the scriptures of the Dragon Palace.
In quiet contemplation of the teachings and their meanings,
the merit accrues to those nearby; yet in exploring the mysteries of the Great Way, [the truth lies far beyond].
Truly, you provide clear guidance;
do not savor the Dharma for its own sake.
I am deeply indebted to your great grace.
I cannot but express my gratitude for your profound benevolence;
yet, I fear it may bring disorder to the King’s transformative governance. Since my return to the country, Xuanzang has been as follows.
Up to the present day,
all those who wear the black robes have deeply rejoiced in seeking the Dharma.
Compassionate toward his tattered robes,
he generously bestowed monastic garments upon him;
today, there are three cassocks in his possession.
Ten bolts of silk gauze bestowed by Your Majesty’s grace,
as well as embroidered images, colored banners, and various ritual implements for offerings obtained from various temples,
are enclosed along with this brief letter.
I respectfully inquire after my teachers and friends.
I request that you convey this message to India by means of the current envoy,
hoping that through this reliance and trust I may express my gratitude for your profound kindness.
Thus, may the wind of benevolence and righteousness illuminate the state,
and my humble and ignorant aspirations be fulfilled.
I am unable to contain the sincerity of my devotion to your virtue.
I respectfully submit this memorial to present my petition for Your Majesty’s consideration.
I humbly pray that Your Sacred Benevolence will graciously grant me favor and permission.
I respectfully conclude.

In the evening, each time he visited the temple, he would compose verses to express his feelings. When the Emperor was still in the position of Crown Prince, he visited the Great Ci’en Monastery and stayed in the quarters of Dharma Master Xuanzang, composing the following verse while observing the Hall of Blessings: *Stopping the carriage to gaze upon the Hall of Blessings.*
As my gaze wanders, I behold the imperial majesty:
the Wheel of Dharma turns as it embraces the sun,
and the floral canopy soars in connection with the clouds.
Emerald mist perfumes the exquisite pavilion;
vermilion clouds illuminate the precious robes.
The rainbow-like banners distantly hold their colors.
The void and water are clearly distinguished in their radiance;
serenely ascending the ten stages,
one spontaneously attains the convergence of the three refuges.
Memorial for the Presentation of Scriptures. Memorial submitted by the śramaṇa Xuanzang:
The aforementioned scriptures and the *Prātimokṣa* are truly the essential pivot for the initial arousal of the bodhicitta.
It serves as a bridge and ferry across the difficult straits;
by reciting it or merely hearing its name,
one obtains immeasurable merit.
I pray for your profound and secret assistance to forever preserve the sacred person of the Emperor.
I respectfully present this offering,
and my heart is filled with deep trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.
A Memorial Requesting the Sanskrit Manuscripts. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang:
Regarding the aforementioned sūtras, vinayas, and other texts...
These are all the tracks of the five vehicles and the profound essentials of the Tripiṭaka;
both their textual expressions and meanings are vast.
The disciples held him in profound reverence.
Xuanzang traveled to the Western Regions,
where he searched everywhere for lost texts.
Of the various scriptures obtained, there are some six hundred fascicles remaining;
the aforementioned sūtras and vinayas have not yet arrived.
As for the circulation of the Great Dharma:
There are some things not yet fully understood;
they all currently exist in the kingdom of Khotan,
preserved there exactly as they were.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty,
governing the realm as the Heavenly Sovereign,
has brilliantly inaugurated the Great Way.
He received the mandate and the celestial charts to propagate the True Dharma;
those from distant lands and diverse species came to court after traversing multiple translations of their tongues.
The King of the Tufan of Khotan has now submitted to Your Majesty’s sacred transformation.
We humbly pray that you will issue an imperial decree to dispatch him;
the time for translation is approaching.
Since the benefit conferred is so vast,
I venture to present this memorial; yet, in doing so,
I fear I have lightly offended Your Majesty’s august dignity.
I prostrate myself in increasing trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.

The Eighteen Characters of the Flying-White Script (Feibai Shu) Written by the Emperor for Dharma Master Xuanzang: "Your Reverence is advanced in years and currently suffering from heat; this place is small and cramped. How is your health? Have you finished the translation yet? [Imperial] Decree.
A Memorial of Gratitude for Receiving All the Scriptures The Śramaṇa Xuanzang humbly states:
I have privately examined the holy teachings of the Tripiṭaka;
they are truly a precious mirror that illuminates the truth for those lost in delusion.
A vessel for crossing the ocean of craving;
a sublime cause for entering pure wisdom;
a wondrous path for proceeding toward Bodhi.
Thus, the assembly of monks broke their own bones to manifest the sincerity of their quest for the Dharma;
on the Snowy Mountains, they cast themselves down.
This is to express the celebration of having heard this sutra.
We humbly beseech Your Majesty, the Emperor:
The Golden Wheel governs the realm,
and the transformation through the Ten Wholesome Deeds becomes ever more renewed;
the civil grace unifies the heavens.
The wind of the Eightfold Noble Path fanned ever more vigorously;
although the affairs of the myriad regions were vast,
the practice of *dāna* (generosity) never faltered.
Although administrative affairs are numerous and complex,
my mind never ceases its pursuit of the profound mystery.
I have previously issued a clear edict.
He dispatched [artists] to create all the scriptures,
desiring that the golden words be inscribed upon white silk,
not merely confined to the Crane Grove.
Opening the jade palace amidst frosty spirals—
how could this be merely the Deer Park?
Incense-sandalwood is used to craft the rollers.
It eclipses the fragrance of the campaka flower;
its embroidered binding and cut covers surpass the brilliance of fresh rosy clouds.
Magnificent and revered,
every detail is subtle and exquisite,
such that the virtue of the human king reaches its ultimate fulfillment.
Furthermore, he proclaimed the grace of Heaven,
expressing compassion for Xuanzang’s ignorance as he entered the Dragon Palace.
By the grace of being permitted to retain and recite [this scripture], the sublime Dharma of sweet dew has,
by a stroke of fortune, reached even this humble thatched dwelling.
The divine mani-jewel,
though it gathers within a humble snail-shell dwelling,
is worn upon the head with joy.
Not knowing the parable,
he immediately burned incense and scattered flowers,
and then received, upheld, and recited it.
May the merit generated by this aspiration adorn Your Majesty,
equaling the brilliance of the sun and moon.
Life-span is equalized with the two polarities of heaven and earth;
transformation permeates the three thousandfold world-systems;
and the Way encompasses all that lies beyond the external.
I am unable to contain the height of my joy and gratitude.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks.
The limitations of paper and ink are easily exhausted.
My gratitude is beyond words. I respectfully submit this.

A Memorial of Thanks for Permitting the Composition of the Stele Inscription for Da Ci’en Temple and for Receiving the Assistance of the Prime Minister in Translating the Scriptures The Śramaṇa Xuanzang addresses the Throne: [Text follows]
On the twenty-fourth day of this month,
Wang Junde, an Inner Attendant, respectfully proclaimed an oral edict granting permission to erect a stele for the temple pagoda and to compose its inscription.

Furthermore, he dispatched the Vice President of the Left Yu Zhining, the Director of the Secretariat Lai Ji, the Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong, the Attendant-in-Ordinary Xue Yuanchao, Du Zhenglun, the Assistant Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu, the State Academy Doctor Fan Jun, and other scholars to serve as supervisors for the joint translation of the scriptures.
The profound moisture flows secretly;
the mysterious wind is once again proclaimed.
I reverently uphold these compassionate injunctions.
Joy and apprehension mingle within my breast;
all those among the monastic community cannot help but rejoice.
I, Xuanzang, have heard this.
The sagely virtue is boundless;
the divine efficacy is unfathomable.
Having already expounded the transformation of non-action, it...
It must open the gates to all wonders.
Since the Great Master grew weary of the mundane world,
the Benevolent One has ceased his governance.
The shadow remains on Vulture Peak;
the image transforms and its transmission becomes empty.
The crane-tree conceals its sound.
These subtle words have truly been spread abroad;
were it not for the Sovereign Radiance emerging from the Thunderous Mandate and the Sage Wisdom ascending the Chart,
who would deliver the Way to the four classes of living beings?
His wisdom encompasses the three realms of existence.
How is it that he is able to concentrate his thoughts on the realm of the profound ford and direct his mind toward the path of Great Enlightenment?
You entice weary merchants toward the transformation of the city and rescue wandering children from perilous dwellings.
We humbly reflect upon Your Majesty, the Emperor.
Holding the scales to compile auspiciousness,
grasping the mandate to ride upon the times,
he nurtures and gives birth to the Three Spirits.
He molds and fashions the myriad things;
those far away find peace and those nearby arrive.
The seas are tranquil and the rivers clear.
The grasses and trees take on a firm integrity;
the mists and clouds shift their hues.
With his hands folded in formal ease, he enjoys abundant leisure.
His thoughts range across the groves of words;
his principles transcend the Three Mysteries,
and his prose excels the Seven Orbits.
Since the propagation and salvation afforded by the sublime scriptures of Śākyamuni predominate,
my heart is set upon their perpetuation and flourishing; may you therefore deign to provide profound assistance from above.
Desiring to personally bestow your sagely refinement and formally select your profound principles,
you have issued detailed edicts to the eminent scholars of the court.
The sublime Dharma was proclaimed and permitted to spread;
the teaching of the Image Age reached the East for over five hundred years,
and although its essential purport was extensively expounded.
Although there have been many generations [of such figures],
the honor of providing such brilliant assistance rests uniquely upon this day.
The devas and humans were filled with joy;
Heaven and Earth harmonized in celebration.
The Golden Wheel was now in motion.
The Jade Calendar is thus eternally enduring.
Such being the case,
the Emperor of Han’s elegant compositions—
Emperor Wu of the Wei dynasty, a man of extraordinary talent, merely composed his literary works at Wuhui,
while [the Master] expounded his thoughts on the Fen River.
There has never yet been one who, wielding this grand pen,
has assisted those profound regulations,
penetrating the three realms to spread their fame far and wide.
It traverses the six realms of darkness to bestow moisture and nourishment;
thus it causes the brilliant sun of wisdom to borrow the sacred brushstrokes to increase its radiance.
The wriggling and deluded living beings,
upon beholding the celestial words, awakened to the Way; I,
Xuanzang, have fortunately encountered this auspicious era.
Having long since donned the monastic robes,
my virtue falls short of that of Senghui,
and my practice pales in comparison to that of Falan.
I have repeatedly received your extraordinary favor,
for which I am constantly filled with deep awe and trepidation; once again, I reverently acknowledge your gracious encouragement.
My awe and trepidation increase all the more;
I am unable to contain the utmost depth of my gratitude and indebtedness.
I respectfully approach the palace to present this memorial.
I respectfully submit this expression of gratitude for your consideration. I humbly state:
A Memorial Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang in Gratitude for Receiving the Stele Inscription of Da Ci’en Monastery. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang states: [text continues]

Having received the official notice from the Court of State Ceremonial, I prostrate myself in submission to the Imperial Decree, wherein Your Majesty has personally inscribed these characters with your own brush.
The inscription composed for the Great Ci'en Monastery has been completed;
His Majesty’s grace extends everywhere,
and his imperial words shine down with particular brilliance.
The Gate of Mystery becomes ever more exalted,
and the companions of the Brahma-faith increase in glory;
I stand upon this vast earth, filled with shame.
Bearing the vast heavens yet possessing but meager strength—
thus I, Xuanzang, have heard:
such is the work of the Creator.
Since the sages cultivated the teachings by ordering all things,
the Way of the Sages is likewise revealed through language to manifest their inner sentiments.

Thus, the drawing of the trigrams and the hanging of the written texts were empty talk regarding physical forms and vessels; the establishment of the lines and the division of the images [were likewise so].
Yet, even within the confines of this realm,
the virtue of the August Emperor is still praised throughout the ages of antiquity.
The character of the royal consorts remains uniquely superior to that of later generations;
how could it be compared to those who "open up things and accomplish affairs"?
He expounded the Eightfold Noble Path to manifest the sublime teachings;
he established words to elucidate the Way and realized the Three Insights to guide the world.
Its principles exhaust what lies beyond heaven and earth;
its sentiments encompass what is outside the sun and moon.
When comparing their relative merits:
This is truly magnificent.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty, the Emperor, wields the Golden Wheel and rides upon the auspicious timing of the Jade Calendar.
Your transformative influence overflows across the four continents;
your benevolence extends throughout the nine realms.
Your Way encompasses both the sages and the holy ones.
His merit flourished to the point of divinity;
he exercised manifold abilities through innate knowledge,
for his natural endowment was derived from the ultimate reach of Heaven.
She first mourned for her bridal mirror and immediately established a temple; in no time,
she raised a sublime banner of victory.
Furthermore, regarding the literary regulations:
when celestial blossoms burst forth in brilliance and sagely compositions surge like waves.
It swallows the ocean of scriptural writings to conceive the Dragon Palace;
it obscures the forest of eloquence to encompass the Crane Tree.
Within, it comprehends the Eight Treasuries.
Externally, it encompasses the Six Classics;
it is profound yet canonical, vast yet subtle.
Thus, the vestiges of the Jetavana Garden,
relying on precious thoughts, become ever more sublime;
the lingering fragrance of the Āmrapālī Grove—
Relying upon these exquisite compositions, one remains undeluded;
they do more than merely elevate one from the realm of dreams—
they illuminate the path of the lost.
I trust that you, who mold and pattern the four heavens and encompass the three realms, have taken me— Xuanzang—
whose words and deeds are devoid of merit, yet who has vulgarly joined the ranks of the monastic community,
under your gracious consideration.
I have always considered myself most fortunate to be further blessed by your profound grace in accomplishing this work,
and to have joyfully encountered the flourishing of the Semblance Dharma.
Feeling both shame and joy,
these emotions truly intermingle within my heart;
I am unable to contain my utmost sincerity of reverent veneration.
I respectfully approach the Imperial Court to present this memorial in expression of my gratitude.
I humbly state.
A Memorial Requesting the Inscription for the Stele of the Great Ci’en Monastery. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang states:
I humbly consider that [the Buddha] manifests signs in response to sentient beings.
The Divine employs all-encompassing breadth;
He establishes teachings according to the times.
Thus, the Sage’s meritorious work reaches its ultimate fulfillment.

Thus we know that only when both the sun and moon shine brightly do they fully exhaust the movement of traversing the heavens; only when both grasses and trees flourish together do they reach the ultimate limit of the virtue of beautifying the earth.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty,
the Emperor, possesses wisdom that encompasses all things and benevolence that moistens the three realms;
thus, you have greatly flourished the sublime transformation.
Furthermore, he propagated the profound wind of our tradition,
regarding with disdain the Zhou kings' fondness for the Way and their empty appreciation of the odes sung at the Yaochi Pond.
Disregarding the profound reverence for the Dharma by Emperor Ming of Han and Emperor Xiaowu of Song,
they merely established the shrine of the White Horse;
thus, the Heavenly Texts were subsequently brought down from above.
To propagate far-reaching the profound purport,
we have carved it upon a magnificent jade tablet,
so that its flourishing principles may long endure.
It shares the resonance of the Six Harmonies and the brilliance of the Five Planets;
it spreads supreme virtue and moves the common people.
He propagated great vows to rectify the age;
how could he have been merely one who secretly assisted the *tathatā* and revealed the profound mysteries?
Although his elegant discourse has already flourished and is about to be engraved upon jade tablets, [the task remains incomplete].
Yet the silver hooks have not yet been inscribed,
and the vermilion characters remain concealed within.
Thus, while the musical instruments have already been set upon their stands.
It is not that the narrow lanes and crooked alleys are worthy of inclusion;
once the dragon’s resonance has ceased,
how can the torchlight of a mere firefly illuminate anything?
Were it not for Ya Kuang tuning the pitch-pipes and Yi He guiding the chariot,
how could the great sound of the Dharma drum be raised,
or the radiant colors of the Sun of Wisdom be augmented?
Daring to rely upon this principle,
I venture to employ it for my prayer.
I humbly entreat that you will deign to inscribe these extolled virtues with Your Divine Brush.
May its subtle excellence surpass the clouds and its traces exceed those of former kings;
may the marvels of its "hanging dew" calligraphy endure.
His fragrance soared after the Sage;
like the golden sound and the jade resonance,
he immediately awakened the multitude of deluded beings.
With its phoenix soaring and dragon coiling,
it shall open the eyes of the many who are blind;
how could it merely cause the flourishing of the Buddha’s teachings as in the era of Yao?
All living beings receive the greatest of favors;
indeed, they truly contribute to the brilliance of this enlightened era,
and the ancestral altars enjoy eternal blessings.
I, Xuanzang, am of dull and shallow intellect;
by error, I have been numbered among the ranks of the monastic forest. I have always felt ashamed of my own limited learning and explorations.
Thanks to your observance of the Vinaya,
you have humbled yourself by deigning to address me with imperial words, and have been excessively honored by your gracious praise.
Although my alarm and trepidation are extreme and I find no place to set my face,
I have for many days been diligent in my devotion and uplifted in my sincerity; thus,
I venture once more to trouble you with this petition.

I harbor even greater awe, as if dwelling in icy valleys. I respectfully submit this statement.
