I have humbly received the Imperial Decree,
which graciously permits me to inscribe the text of the Imperial Composition for the Great Ci'en Monastery using the Emperor’s own calligraphy.
The imperial edict has now arrived.
Your compassionate decree has been humbly bestowed upon me;
I receive it with profound reverence, shame,
and trepidation, not knowing how to respond.
Xuanzang has heard that when a powerful crossbow is drawn to the full,
even a field mouse is insufficient to trigger its mechanism.
The great bell conceals its sound;
without the subtle touch of a striker, it has no means to manifest its resonance.
Yet, one cannot say that the sun does not approach or the moon does not shine upon it.
He then turned his focus toward the Gate of Emptiness;
like rain moistening thick clouds,
he manifested a profound resonance within the Mysterious Temple.
This is what I have prayed for;
how could it have been my intention?
I humbly beseech Your Majesty to tread upon the wings of the sun and ascend the pivot of the universe.
He grasped the mandate to continue the legacy of antiquity,
surpassing Xuan and outstripping Xu;
he encompassed the Xia and swallowed up the Yin.
He manifested a multitude of wonders to transform the age;
he synthesized manifold abilities to illuminate the world.
Within the nine provinces, all have been bathed in the breeze of benevolence;
beyond the four heavens as well, they have been moistened by profound transformation.
Such being the case, as for the Dharma that serves as a bridge and raft—
Were it not for the Most Holy One, there would be no one to fully elucidate its source;
were it not for the Most Venerable One, how could the work of profound assistance manifest its traces?
Although the utmost limit of honoring the distant ancestors moves the natural feelings of Heaven,
blessings from the unseen may still be prayed for; therefore,
please turn Your Imperial gaze toward this end.
The sublime verses and lyrics have already surpassed the rarities of past ages; now that the secret traces are revealed,
they shall be widely disseminated.
It was like a treasure of exceeding value about to be bestowed;
among all classes of beings, there were none who did not rejoice and pay homage.
Yet, those followers of the Brahma-faring life rejoiced with even greater exuberance.
To dream of the grand music of the Celestial Emperor is not extraordinary upon returning from it;
yet to obtain the crest-jewel of a Wheel-Turning King is truly marvelous.
How could such a thing be considered noble?
It is my hope that it shall be engraved upon true stone and erected within the courtyard of merit.
Those deluded beings, still crawling in ignorance,
are now having their ears and eyes opened;
the torch of the Dharma blazes forth in full splendor.
May it be transmitted to future generations,
so that those who behold these precious characters may aspire toward the silver calligraphy [of the Buddhas],
and awaken the bodhicitta on this very day.
By reciting his bequeathed writings, one may explore their profound mysteries;
herein, one awakens to Prajñā, where the city of kalpas is exhausted within a mustard seed.
The brilliant beauty endures forever;
though seas shift and mulberry trees encircle the land,
the flourishing wind remains undecaying.
Xuanzang was born of common stock and has long felt ashamed of his own lack of spiritual practice; now that I have been granted the tonsure,
I am filled with gratitude.
Seeking to propagate the profound Way,
he traveled to Kapilavastu; fundamentally,
he relied upon the imperial transformation.
Now that this translation has been completed,
I have once again received the rewards of the Imperial Court;
it was during the era of the Zhenguan reign that—
I have unworthily basked in your vast benevolence; since the Yonghui era,
I have further received this extraordinary favor.
By the divine brush of the two sovereigns,
you have humbly granted the exaltation of the sacred compositions of two reigns.
That you have bestowed upon me these magnificent decorations is something for which I, a person of humble and inferior capacity,
truly feel deep apprehension and fear.
The sincerity of repaying this debt of gratitude has never been forgotten, from dusk until dawn; yet,
it is simply because the depth of your kindness is so vast and profound.
How could a drop of water ever repay such profound generosity?
Even a lofty mountain peak cannot suffice to express gratitude for even a speck of dust.
One should rely solely on the power of various forms of wisdom to operate with unimpeded means,
thereby enhancing the imperial mausoleum and assisting in the consolidation of the foundation for seven hundred years.
I am unable to contain my utmost sense of reverence and veneration.

I respectfully entrust this memorial of thanks to the Inner Attendant, Your Servant Wang Junde, to present for Your Majesty’s perusal. I beg forgiveness for the presumption of intruding upon Your Majesty’s august presence.
I prostrate myself in profound trepidation. This is my humble submission.

A Memorial of Gratitude for the Presentation of the Stele Inscription of the Great Ci’en Monastery and the Performance of the Ninefold Music. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang addresses the Throne: [Your Majesty] has graciously sent the stele inscription of the Great Ci’en Monastery and provided the performance of the ninefold music. I am deeply moved by this imperial bounty and offer my heartfelt thanks. Respectfully submitted.
On the fourteenth day of this month,
we have humbly received the imperial decree sending the Imperially Composed and Calligraphed Text for the Stele of the Great Ci’en Monastery.
Furthermore, the ninefold musical offerings were performed as an act of worship;
like the sun of Yao dividing its light,
they first increased the brilliance of the torch of wisdom.
The waves of the sea of Śākyamuni’s teachings flow everywhere,
further augmenting the vastness of the stream of Dharma;
magnificent monuments are erected upon the cliffs.
The celestial lights shine like the hues of a multicolored sunset reflecting upon a sacred mountain;
one might suspect that the dense constellations have descended upon a divine peak.
All those present, both monastics and laypeople,
were as startled and rushed as lightning and thunder;
they gazed upon him with awe and leaped for joy at such an unprecedented occurrence.
I venture to say that the Eight Trigrams suspended their written patterns,
and the Six Lines gave rise to the appended explanations.
Observing the birds, he established the laws;
weeping for the qilin, he spread the canons.
These are the noble deeds of the Sage.
All these are fully manifested herein. Thus,
by modeling objects to establish patterns and instituting teachings according to the times, [the Way is preserved].
He molds and refines all living beings and restrains or elevates the spirit of the times. Thus,
when the First Emperor of Qin engraved his inscriptions upon stone, [he proclaimed:]...
Only the rites of feng and shan manifest their beauty;
the stele erected by the Wei sovereign merely records his achievements at Dayang.
To merely cite the title and look down upon the kings of a hundred generations—
how could this compare to personally receiving the refined compositions of Your Majesty’s sagacious pen?
Bending down, he unfurled the immortal calligraphy;
the golden music released its melody,
and the silver hooks dazzled with their traces.
He explored the Dragon Palace to construct the Three Mysteries and surpassed the Phoenix Script to exhaust the Eight Calligraphic Styles;
he galloped his thoughts like surging spring waves.
He distills the essence of autumn dew to manifest his uniqueness;
he propagates the wondrous principles of the One Vehicle and extols the profound mysteries of the Six Perfections.
His transformations pervade the entire realm of the three thousandfold world system;
his fame resounds beyond ten billion lands.
The subtle words of the Pomegranate Grove—
Borrowing the terminology of the heavens, it is made even more manifest;
the Bodhisattva of the Bamboo Grove,
relying upon the divine brush, is rendered all the more venerable.
Thus, he caused the brahmins to take refuge in his heart;
they severed the net of doubt and reverently received his instruction,
while Pāpīyān transformed his thoughts.
By leveling the crooked mountains and smoothing the path,
how could it merely allow those within the gates of dust to finally realize they had lost their way?
A guest from the realm of dreams,
his practice transcended the limits of suffering;
when the Image-Dharma gradually spread to the East.
Approaching six hundred years in age,
the grandeur of its propagation and elucidation has never been as great as it is now.
As for Emperor Ming of the Han, who attained spiritual resonance,
he still consulted with Fu Yi; and as for the Ruler of Wu,
who turned toward and revered [the Dharma],...
It was as if one were resolving doubts with Kan Ze;
from that time downward,
there has been no one worthy of mention.
Transforming beings in accordance with conditions,
he alone promotes the auspicious destiny;
when one does good, there must be a response.
He has firmly established a magnificent foundation,
like a sovereign of the Golden Wheel;
his divine achievements are unfathomable.
Like an Emperor wearing the precious crown,
his glorious reign shall endure forever. I,
Xuanzang, have by error been graced with the imperial favor.
Fortunately, I have ascended to this profound marketplace,
where the clouds once again gather and the Dharma drum is struck anew.
Now that the transformation through the Three Clarities has flourished and the gateway of the Eightfold Noble Path remains perpetually open,
I reflect upon my own lack of sincere devotion.
I, Xū, have forever been graced by your guidance;
looking up to the high heavens, I am indebted for your bounty,
while gazing down at the deep valley, I am filled with shame.
Inexpressibly moved by a heart of profound veneration,
I respectfully approach the Hall of Audience to submit this memorial of thanks; for having disturbed Your Majesty’s imperial presence,
I am filled with deep trepidation and alarm.
Respectfully submitted.

A memorial requesting that Dharma Master Shanno and others be permitted to receive full ordination again. Memorial by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang: [The text continues with the formal address and the petition.]
I have humbly received the gracious imperial decree granting ordination to Shanluo and others;
my joy is boundless and cannot be fully expressed.
With both sorrow and joy reaching me, I have humbly reflected that even the grace of clouds and rain still relies upon the vessel from which it flows,
and even the illumination of the sun and moon still encounters obstacles when falling upon an overturned bowl.
Yet, the waves of grace from Your Majesty, the Sage Emperor, have now extended even beyond the furthest shores.
The supreme benevolence and gracious favor of Your Majesty, the Emperor and Empress Dowager,
truly transcend the bounds of the ordinary. We humbly submit this.
He embodies the numinous and wondrous awakening and manifests traces through skillful means; thus,
he is able to discern the ultimate reality of True Suchness.
Turning the Wheel of Dharma throughout the nine realms of existence,
he compassionately embraces all classes of beings and rescues those submerged in suffering within the three miserable paths.
Consequently, Shanluo, Fatong, Chuchu, Yan,
and others were able to once again wash away the celestial waves and re-emerge under the sacred sun.
They traverse the Yellow Springs to ascend the Clear Milky Way;
they push aside the burning house to be shaded by the Dharma Clouds.
The boulder is cast back and vanishes into emptiness.
This grace shall be imperishable,
while my humble person will merely perish;
by what means can I repay this?
May the merit of shaving the hair cause afflictions to vanish within the imperial palace;
may the power of the full precepts [bring about this result].
I present these blessings upon the fragrant path.
I humbly pray that the Emperor and Empress may enjoy ten thousand springs of longevity.
May his radiant brilliance, the fruit of a hundred blessings,
long preside over the Purple Pole and forever shelter all living beings.
Prince Kaku-mo of the Spring Palace spreads his brilliance like soaring blossoms;
favored by the azure realm, he rules over his noble fief.
His virtue has been further exalted upon the great rock,
and his fragrance has spread throughout the imperial palace;
as Xuanzang reflects upon this within myself, I am filled with humility.
I possess no virtue for my time and no merit for my country,
yet I have been unworthily bathed in extraordinary favor.
As the years have accumulated,
when has he not been distressed?
His shadow is ashamed and his spirit ceases its activity.
Eating and forgetting to sleep until exhaustion,
the bamboo of the Xiang River would not suffice to exhaust my gratitude;
were one to sacrifice bodies as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who could ever repay such a bounty?
I still rely upon the imperial favor to sustain my life for a while;
I am overwhelmed by the utmost gratitude.
I respectfully submit this appended memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
Having troubled Your Imperial Majesty’s sight,
I am filled with increasing trepidation.
Respectfully stated.
A Memorial of Thanks for Receiving Medical Treatment. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang states:
Xuanzang has been unskilled in maintaining my own health.
The cold urticaria flared up again,
nearly becoming chronic and severe;
he was on the verge of departing from the auspicious reign.
By Your Majesty’s compassionate grace,
an excellent physician has been sent down; as soon as the acupuncture and medicine were applied, [the ailment was cured].
He immediately received healing;
his failing years were halted at the brink of exhaustion,
and his solitary soul was restored just as it was about to perish.
Beholding once more this prosperous age and again following the enlightened guidance,
how could it be that my chronic ailments are not forever severed?
My principles have been constantly regulated by this alone. Yet,
reflecting upon my own meager and unworthy self,
I have repeatedly received extraordinary grace.
The favors bestowed were profound while my life was precarious;
I knew not how to repay them,
relying solely upon the power of wisdom.
I hope to repay these profound blessings;
yet, Xuanzang remains physically frail and exhausted,
and am as yet unable to proceed to the imperial palace to offer my thanks.
I am unable to express the utmost depth of my reverent veneration.
I respectfully dispatch my disciple, Mahāyānaprabha, to present this memorial for Your Majesty’s information.
Respectfully stated.
A Memorial of Thanks for Receiving Medicine and the Imperial Envoy’s Inquiry after Illness. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang speaks:
I, Xuanzang, am beset by the accumulation of karmic burdens.
This brought upon him the suffering of illness;
at the moment of his final breath,
he was nearly separated from the light of day.
Suddenly, we have been graced by the Emperor and Empress’s descent of compassionate thoughts and their concern for our very lives;
celestial messengers have arrived repeatedly with their instructions.
There are more than ten consolations;
divine medicine looks down to save us—
if we encounter even a single pill.
Having drunk from and bathed in Your Sacred Compassion,
my deep anguish has already been dispelled;
I am deeply grateful for the medical care I have received.
Thus, he was completely healed.
Who would have expected that his departed soul would be summoned by the Supreme Deity,
so that the longevity of Heaven might be received once more from the Great Furnace?
I withdraw in self-reflection upon my own meager and humble nature;
how could I possibly be worthy of this?
I beat my breast in profound shame and distress.
Words are insufficient to proclaim it;
how could I ever be worthy of such extraordinary grace?
Even if I were to grind my humble body to dust, I would still fail to express my gratitude.
I now hope to exert myself in this ritual recitation,
exhausting both body and mind,
to repay your invaluable kindness.
I have, in small measure, stilled my boundless debt of gratitude.
Feeling a sense of profound thankfulness beyond measure,
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks.
My joy and fear are intertwined, leaving me utterly at a loss for what to do. I respectfully submit this memorial.

Memorial Submitted to Thank the Monks and Nuns for the Suspension of the Provisions Requiring Them to Follow Secular Laws The Śramaṇa Xuanzang speaks: [I humbly thank the monks and nuns for the suspension of the provisions requiring them to follow secular laws.]
I have humbly observed the Imperial Decree regarding the provision that monks and nuns who commit offenses shall be suspended from the application of secular laws.
Returning to the established regulations,
an unmerited bounty has suddenly been bestowed upon the assembly of monastics.
Unexpected grace has once again reached these humble quarters;
we gaze toward the sun and bathe in the Way.
Your practical brilliance illuminates all;
we crouch upon the ground and humble ourselves,
feeling nothing but increasing trepidation.
I humbly consider that since the Dharma King has passed away,
the transmission of the semblance-dharma has become empty; the regulations for its veneration and succession—
I entrust this to all wise sovereigns.
I humbly beseech Your Majesty, the Emperor, that as the precious orb ascends the throne,
you may mount the True Golden Wheel.
Looking back upon this teaching of Śākyamuni,
I am deeply moved to propagate and expound it;
for I consider that shedding worldly adornments is the gateway to the profound mystery.
He fundamentally differed from worldly customs;
although his conduct was often deficient due to being entangled by the five turbidities,
he remained clothed in the three robes.
The field of merit lies herein.
He has severed the dense web of jade-like regulations and spread forth broad benevolence,
placing his trust in the true words of the Golden Mouth.
May this dedication be granted;
thus, the celestial deities will surely be delighted and respond with auspicious omens.
Not only would my fellow monks cherish this kindness,
but it is further augmented by its steadfastness;
were one to turn their back on such magnanimity, [they would incur great fault].
To bring such calamity upon oneself would be to contravene the solemn decree of the Great Master and to diminish the profound compassion of the Holy Sovereign.
All those who are enlightened and numinous should naturally mete out condemnation and punishment;
why wait for the laws of judicial review and rectification?
Now that the crime of wickedness and recklessness is being formally adjudicated,
I, Xuanzang, am a man of mediocre and dull wit, yet I have unworthily been included within the stream of the Dharma.
Each time I have been graced by your vast bounty,
I have already harbored feelings of shame and trepidation;
now, once again, I receive these extraordinary rewards.
I am once again filled with trepidation;
however, as I have recently been afflicted by illness,
I have been unable to follow the established custom of attending at the palace gate.
Inexpressibly moved by a heart of profound veneration, I respectfully dispatch my disciple Dàchéngguāng to present this memorial of thanks. I humbly submit this report.
谨言 (Jǐnyán) — Respectfully stated.
A Memorial of Grateful Thanks for the Imperial Decree Regarding the Suspension of the Application of Secular Laws to Monks and Nuns. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang addresses Your Majesty:
I have humbly received the gracious imperial decree.
Aside from the articles concerning the examination of monks and nuns according to secular law,
the sincerity with which they wear [the precepts] is beyond the reach of any known analogy.
I have humbly examined how the True Dharma flourishes and is extolled,
rising and falling in accordance with those above; thus, the constant patterns of human relations are either thinned or strengthened.
To emulate the profound style of the Dark Sage and restore what was deficient:
since the auspicious destiny of the Sage resided within us, the Radiant Emperor has upheld the pure essence,
honoring and exalting the Way and its arts.
Distinguishing between the profound and the mundane,
he opens the key to non-duality and broadens the track of the sole principle.
The Dragon Palace was transcribed upon the Penglai Pavilion;
the Vulture Peak territory was joined to this sacred ground,
so that the resonant sounds of the Dharma might overflow throughout the realm.
The meritorious karma of blessings bathes the common people;
this is truly a magnificent assembly of the Dharma-gate,
a source of great fortune for all within the realm.
The conduct of the monastic community under [his] leadership was disordered; his instructions and governance were contrary to the proper method,
thereby causing internal detriment to the Buddha-dharma.
When one person externally violates the king’s law,
the entire multitude suffers the resulting calamity.
Consequently, he incurred the imperial majesty and was ordered to follow secular law;
what had been expected was a state of pure solemnity.
My intent was to issue a warning;
the monks were struck with awe and fear,
feeling ashamed and humbled day and night.
Yet the sagely discernment presides like Heaven,
and benevolent grace shines forth universally;
he establishes profound expectations upon the realm of the mysterious and wondrous.
Encompassing even the slightest taint within its vast magnanimity,
it has bestowed extraordinary grace and commuted this severe punishment.
It was not that the man himself was to be pitied;
rather, it was because this Dharma is worthy of veneration.
Thus, the fish caught in the net were enabled to swim once more in the Yangtze and Han rivers.
A bird trapped in a cage soars back into the profound void; the waters of the Dharma,
though turbid, become clearer still, and the saline fields of merit are restored to fertility.
May each member of the Sangha deeply feel this burden of responsibility;
may those who observe us strive with diligence.
It is my hope that you will exert your resolve to abandon all evil.
To accord with the Will of Heaven,
I shall focus my mind on ritual worship and recitation,
thereby repaying this great bounty.
I humbly pray that the Emperor and Empress, by virtue of their merit in propagating and upholding the Dharma, may eternally concentrate a hundred blessings;
and riding upon the karma of compassion,
may they rule with effortless ease for ten thousand springs.
Auspicious signs have been established within the realm,
and the defensive walls of the state are fully adorned with excellence. I cannot restrain my boundless joy and profound gratitude.
I respectfully submit this appended table to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
To thus lightly trouble Your Imperial Majesty is a source of profound trepidation.
Respectfully stated.
Memorial of Thanks for the Bestowal of Linen and Miscellaneous Items. A Memorial of Thanks for the Bestowal of Linen and Miscellaneous Items. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang.
You have graciously bestowed upon me linen and various other items.
Holding it in my hands, I was struck with awe and shame;
I did not know how to describe it by analogy.
Moreover, it was a garment of golden thread.
Transmitted from former sages;
or perhaps it is a priceless precious robe,
as heard in the sacred scriptures.
There has never been one who exhausted the mysteries and perfected the subtleties, perceiving them at a glance as if they were in the palm of his hand,
such as this present gift. Observing its even colors and its subtle,
refined essence, even Jingjun could not surpass its merit.
The tailoring is elegant and meticulous;
one cannot discern the seams even amidst the intricate inlays.
Instantly, it feels as though mist and clouds have entered the chamber.
The orchid garden resides within one's person;
when one looks down upon it,
its splendor and value suddenly increase.
In the past, Dao’an was called a "Jewel" during the Qin dynasty,
yet he had not yet encountered such grace;
Zhi Dun was praised as a "Ritual Master" during the Jin dynasty.
Rarely has such grace been heard of;
only I, Xuanzang, being of humble and meager merit, have alone and secretly received this great favor.
Looking back upon these honors, I reflect upon my own person.
My trepidation and perspiration grow ever deeper.
I humbly pray that the Emperor and Empress may have many descendants and enjoy eternal blessings and sovereignty.
May you long gaze upon the jade mirror and forever govern the precious chart;
may you nurture and protect all living beings within the commanderies.
This will endure as long as heaven itself.
Unable to bear the height of my shame and remorse,
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and bring it to Your Majesty’s ears.

I have humbly heard that as the Ultimate Way spreads forth,
it opens the way for celestial and human beings throughout the span of their lifespans.
Profound indeed is what has been thus moved:
that an esoteric sage was born with such precocious wisdom.
I humbly reflect upon this.
The Emperor and Empress have realized the mirror-like clarity of the three voids;
their transformative influence has reached all within the nine realms.
Thus, they are able to lift the hanging tassels of their ceremonial caps to perceive the two truths.
When King Mahāsammata first tasted the grain of the single vehicle,
he thereupon made a koṭi of vows.
While still in the womb,
Xuanke manifested the signs of transcending the city walls,
thereby causing the One of Ten Epithets to descend as a spirit.
May this vast gathering embrace and sustain [the assembly];
may a hundred deities provide protection and assistance, solemnly guarding the precincts of this palace.
Thus, calamities were thoroughly cleansed,
and peace and harmony prevailed; the seven flowers stood solemnly to receive his steps,
and the nine dragons lowered themselves to bathe his form.
The traces of the Mysterious Gate remain poised;
the shade of the Tree of the Way is empty.
Although in the past, treading upon the Emperor’s throne presented auspicious omens, [the present reality remains thus].
Even if one were to feel the heavens to seek out wonders,
how could they suffice to compare with this magnificent bounty or match this illustrious achievement?
Let all the people sing its praises.
We rejoice that the Imperial Throne has received divine protection;
the assembly of monastics is bold and vigorous,
delighted that the Dark-Hoofed Steed has come to roam here.
I humbly pray that you will not forget your former kindness,
but graciously grant that my monastic robes shall not be confined by worldly attachments, so that I may cultivate excellent causes for the future.
Furthermore, as for the exalted status of a prince, the choice between remaining in the world or departing from it lies within your own power.
The station of the Dharma King is increasingly exalted and magnificent; furthermore,
his meritorious virtues are boundless, and his role as a bridge and raft for sentient beings extends far and wide.
If the sagely grace remains unerring and the great vow does not waver,
I venture to suggest that the resources of the four seas be exhausted for this purpose.
The practice of *dāna* cannot compare to this;
even the deeds of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) are insufficient to serve as an analogy for this foundation of merit.
I pray that the Emperor and Empress may have the hundred blessings coalesce into radiant splendor,
their glory equaling the ultimate,
and that ten thousand springs manifest their longevity.
They shall firmly secure the Southern Mountains and exhaust all pleasures throughout their extended lifespans,
traversing the *sāmayika* state across distant kalpas.
The Crown Prince is truly eminent;
he shall pacify and succeed to the imperial enterprise.
It is most fitting that his favor be abundant.
He assisted and illuminated the royal house;
from his earliest years, he was a brilliant scion whose auspicious blessings multiplied ever more abundantly.
He distinguished the branches from the root and continued the fragrant dust upon the grass seat. Xuanzang has,
by overstepping his station, been joined with this great era.
Their shadows are confined within the palace gates;
their nobility does not arise from the elevation of virtue,
but their favor results from the accumulation of personal grace.
Fortunate that we belong to this land at the very commencement of its national celebration,
as the foundation of pure karma is laid;
my heart leaps with joy.
I am free from resentment.
I cannot contain my utmost joy and congratulations.
I respectfully submit this memorial to inform Your Majesty.
A slight touch brings about majesty;
it subdues and destroys the Māras.
Speak with reverence.

A Memorial on the Celebration of the Buddha’s Radiance for Three Days by King Zhou, Together with the Presentation of Robes, Alms Bowl, and Staff. The Śramaṇa Xuanzang says: [Memorial on the Celebration of the Buddha’s Radiance for Three Days by King Zhou, Together with the Presentation of Robes, Alms Bowl, and Staff.]
Xuanzang has heard that the *Book of Changes* praises the principle of daily renewal,
and the *Book of Poetry* extols the boundless strength of descendants.
This is why the Zhou dynasty exceeded its allotted span and the Han calendar endured for so long;
it was in response to this Way.
Furthermore, I have heard that the Dragon Gate whirls and surges;
it is because its source is vast that its flow extends far.
The cassia trees grow in dense clusters;
their roots are deep and their fragrance is pervasive.
We humbly reflect that the imperial destiny has been passed down through successive sagacious emperors.
Circumscribing with repeated compasses and aligning with repeated squares, he accumulated and cultivated benevolence and righteousness,
which gradually permeated the common people.
This has been so for a long time. Thus,
these two sovereigns have gloriously received the Great Treasure,
establishing it as a foundation for their descendants.
It may be said that its roots are deep and its source is long;
now that Your Majesty has received full ordination,
your meritorious achievements will become even more flourishing.
Returning to simplicity and reverting to the fundamental,
he surpassed the tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
he codified rites and composed music.
He transcended the tracks of the Yin and Zhou dynasties;
he did not regard the yellow canopy as a mark of nobility,
but sought instead to bring relief to the hearts of the myriad people.
Seeking clothing before dawn was clear,
he forgot to eat when the sun slanted past noon;
he refined and cultivated the most eminent and wise men.
He arranged the ranks of his officials,
gathered the capable, and dismissed those who committed transgressions,
exerting himself with vigor in the Right Way.
With a single person presiding with hands folded in formality,
ten thousand *li* were cleared of disorder;
this was the height of prosperity even surpassing that of Kings Cheng and Kang.
Not yet having reached this point,
the "Ministerial Clouds" gather in profusion,
and the rivers and seas are without waves.
It is said that Yu Zunfeng and Long Qing have bathed themselves in this transformation. How vast! How sublime!
It is difficult to describe it fully.
Thereupon, the Way was perceived by the celestial vault,
and the luminous deities bestowed their blessings; on an auspicious day of this favorable month, [the ceremony was performed].
The Crown Prince has been born;
the celestial branches flourish extensively,
and the jade blossoms spread ever wider.
Throughout the realm, all living beings rejoice and rely [upon this grace];
as for Xuanzang himself, it is likewise so.
Maintaining a constant state of mind,
how could one merely rejoice in the safety and well-being of the Holy Mother?
Truly, one also delights that the Tathāgata has an heir.
I humbly pray that you will not contradict your previous decree,
but will immediately grant permission for him to leave the household life,
thereby transferring the lineage of a sovereign king.
He became a son of the Dharma King;
donning the Dharma robes,
he was conferred a Dharma name.
He was granted the Three Refuges and enrolled among the ranks of the Sangha, thereby continuing the transformation through images during the Xiang era of the Shaoxing period.
He propagated the profound breeze of the Dharma,
causing the groves of Chan to flourish once more and the gardens of awakening to shine with renewed splendor.
Following the flourishing traces of Viśuddhanetra and treading in the lofty footsteps of Candracchattra,
they sever the two kinds of fetters.
He attains unsurpassed enlightenment;
his form-body is subtle and wondrous,
like that king of mountains.
Adorned with a net of flames that surpasses the sun and moon,
he subsequently spreads the compassionate clouds over the realm of the great trichiliocosm.
Yang Huiju, across billions of continents,
beat the Dharma drum to subdue the celestial Māras and hoisted the banner of victory to crush the non-Buddhists.
He intercepts the surging currents in the ocean of inversion;
he extinguishes the blazing fires on the mountain of depravity;
and he dries up the deep river of afflictions.
He shattered the massive shell of ignorance;
he is the Tamer of Men,
the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
May the spirits of the ancestral temples,
by virtue of their descendant’s blessings, ascend to the other shore.
May the Emperor and Empress [enjoy long life and prosperity].
By virtue of his merit, may he enjoy ten thousand springs;
may he forever hold the divine chart and eternally preside over the nine realms.
Only when you can act in this way may you be called a filial son of the highest order;
only then do you bring honor to your parents.
This is why Śākyamuni abandoned his kingdom to devote himself to bodhi;
how could it be compared to the trivial virtues of Dongping?
Chen Si, with his mediocre talents,
daily debates superiority and inferiority,
and discusses depth and shallowness among his contemporaries.
I have respectfully prepared my robes and taken up my alms bowl,
awaiting the arrival of virtuous guests,
while sweeping the seats and cleansing the ground.
I am unable to contain my utmost joy and consolation at the news that you are about to mount your carriage to cross the boundaries [of our realm].
I respectfully submit this memorial to inform you.
To lightly encounter Your Majesty’s august majesty increases my trepidation and anxiety.
I respectfully submit this.

Yesterday, I received the gracious imperial decree ordering Xuanzang to shave the crown prince, Fuguang,
and further commanding that seven monks be ordained.
The hair that is shaved off is the falling away of the king's afflictions;
the monks who are ordained...
This is the king’s retinue and equipment;
it causes the palace of Pāpīyān to tremble and fills the hearts of those in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens with exultation.
The Great Vow having been proclaimed,
auspicious blessings flourish ever more abundantly;
how could it be thought that such a task was undertaken by the hands of one so humble and lowly?
The celestial countenance may be moved by skillful artifice;
ordinary people may receive entry into the Way through this auspicious assembly.
Those above and below rejoiced and played with it;
grief and joy mingled within them.
I have humbly reflected upon the gravity of this protective guardianship.
That which precedes the swaddling clothes is the cause of liberation;
it begins with the casting off of ornaments.
I humbly reflect that the Way of the Emperor and Empress is concentrated beyond the realm of forms,
while their blessings permeate the world within.
Thus, they have brilliantly opened the gateway to the subtle mystery.
I have cultivated the root of virtue;
my wish is that Your Majesty’s throne receive divine protection and that the royal palace be graced with enduring harmony.
Facing ten billion worlds and the entire realm, he completes a thousand million years of wonders.
The Buddha’s radiance is higher than a child’s breast; it is only fitting that he be nourished.
Virtuous deities guard his person,
and all Buddhas touch his head;
thus he increases the brilliance of his wisdom and the elegance of his countenance.
The entrustment of perpetuating the harmonious and reverent [Dharma] rests upon the newly ordained monks;
their sense of gratitude is already profound.
You should likewise apply yourself with diligence to the path of practice and focus single-mindedly on the observance of precepts,
so as to truly live up to the imperial decree.
I humbly await your acceptance of this meager grass-offering;
my sense of profound gratitude is beyond measure.
I respectfully submit this memorial for your perusal.
Respectfully Submitted.

A Memorial on the Occasion of the One-Month Anniversary of the Birth of Prince Fuguang and the Presentation of Dharma Robes and Other Gifts. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang. Respectfully Submitted. A Memorial on the Occasion of the One-Month Anniversary of the Birth of Prince Fuguang and the Presentation of Dharma Robes and Other Gifts. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang.
I have humbly heard that those with wings swift enough to seize the wind fill the void after but a few days.
He inscribed "Moon Bright Pearl," completing it within ten days;
thus we know his spirit was received from beyond the mundane world.
That which shines with brilliance in the heavens has already manifested its excellence;
it is surely that which refines and renews its beauty.
Only the Prince of Buddha-Light,
by means of supreme goodness, established auspiciousness;
by expounding the Mean and Harmony, he nurtured virtue.
Since his birth at Weiyuan Garden,
the celestial shrines have been moved to gaze upon him;
his sagely spirit purifies the inner vestments.
In rest and in rising, may you receive divine protection;
